verses.1:1: Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
verses.1:2: to the church of God that is in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called as saints, together with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:
verses.1:3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: I give thanks to my God always concerning you for the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:5: that in every respect you were enriched in Him, in all speech and in all knowledge,
verses.1:6: just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you,
verses.1:7: so that you are not lacking in any gift, eagerly awaiting the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:8: who will also confirm you to the end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.1:10: Now I urge you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be fully united in the same mind and in the same judgment.
verses.1:11: For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by Chloe's people that there are quarrels among you.
verses.1:12: Now I mean this, that each one of you says, "I am of Paul," and "I of Apollos," and "I of Cephas," and "I of Christ."
verses.1:13: Has Christ been divided? Paul was not crucified on your behalf, was he? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?
verses.1:14: I give thanks that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
verses.1:15: so that no one may say that you were baptized into my name.
verses.1:16: Now I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
verses.1:17: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the gospel, not with wisdom of speech, so that the cross of Christ might not be made void.
verses.1:18: For the word concerning the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, yet to us who are being saved it is God's power.
verses.1:19: For it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will set aside."
verses.1:20: Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has God not made foolish the wisdom of the world?
verses.1:21: For since in the wisdom of God the world did not come to know God through wisdom, God was well pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.
verses.1:22: For indeed Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
verses.1:23: but we proclaim Christ crucified, to Jews a stumbling block and to Gentiles foolishness,
verses.1:24: yet to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
verses.1:25: Because God's foolishness is wiser than people, and God's weakness is stronger than people.
verses.1:26: For consider your calling, brothers, that not many were wise according to the flesh, not many powerful, not many of noble birth;
verses.1:27: rather, God chose the foolish things of the world so that He might put the wise to shame, and God chose the weak things of the world so that He might put the strong things to shame,
verses.1:28: and the lowly things of the world and the despised things God chose, the things that are not, so that He might bring to nothing the things that are,
verses.1:29: so that no flesh may boast before God.
verses.1:30: Yet from Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became to us wisdom from God, both righteousness and sanctification and redemption,
verses.1:31: so that, just as it is written, "Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord."
verses.2:1: And when I came to you, brothers, I came not with superiority of speech or of wisdom, declaring to you the testimony of God.
verses.2:2: For I resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.
verses.2:3: And I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling,
verses.2:4: and my speech and my proclamation were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
verses.2:5: so that your faith might not be in the wisdom of people, but in the power of God.
verses.2:6: Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature, though a wisdom not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.
verses.2:7: Instead, we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, which has been hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,
verses.2:8: which none of the rulers of this age has understood; for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.2:9: Rather, just as it is written, "Things which eye did not see and ear did not hear, and which did not come up into a human heart, things which God prepared for those who love Him."
verses.2:10: For to us God revealed them through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God.
verses.2:11: For who among people knows the things of a person except the spirit of the person that is in him? So also no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.
verses.2:12: Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things graciously given to us by God,
verses.2:13: which things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to those who are spiritual.
verses.2:14: Now a natural person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are examined spiritually.
verses.2:15: Yet the spiritual person examines all things, while he himself is examined by no one.
verses.2:16: For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him? Yet we have the mind of Christ.
verses.3:1: And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to people of flesh, as to infants in Christ.
verses.3:2: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able. In fact, even now you are still not able,
verses.3:3: for you are still fleshly. For where there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to human ways?
verses.3:4: For whenever someone says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I of Apollos," are you not human beings?
verses.3:5: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, even as the Lord gave to each one.
verses.3:6: I planted, Apollos watered, but God kept causing the growth.
verses.3:7: Consequently, neither the one planting nor the one watering is anything, but God who causes the growth.
verses.3:8: Now the one who plants and the one who waters are one, yet each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
verses.3:9: For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, God's building.
verses.3:10: According to the grace of God that was given to me, like a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another is building upon it. But let each one watch how he builds upon it.
verses.3:11: For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.
verses.3:12: Now if anyone builds upon the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
verses.3:13: each one's work will become evident, for the Day will make it clear, because it is revealed with fire, and the fire itself will test what sort each one's work is.
verses.3:14: If the work that anyone has built upon it remains, he will receive a reward.
verses.3:15: If anyone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss; yet he himself will be saved, but so as through fire.
verses.3:16: Do you not know that you are God's temple, and that God's Spirit dwells in you?
verses.3:17: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and that is what you are.
verses.3:18: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks himself to be wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.
verses.3:19: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. For it is written, "He catches the wise in their craftiness,"
verses.3:20: and again, "The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile."
verses.3:21: So then let no one boast in people. For all things are yours,
verses.3:22: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world or life or death, or things present or things to come, all things are yours,
verses.3:23: yet you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
verses.4:1: In this way let a person consider us: as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries.
verses.4:2: Here, moreover, it is sought in stewards that one be found faithful.
verses.4:3: To me, however, it is the smallest matter that I should be examined by you or by a human court; in fact, I do not even examine myself.
verses.4:4: For I am aware of nothing against myself, yet I am not justified by this; the One who examines me is the Lord.
verses.4:5: Therefore do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both illuminate the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts; and then praise will come to each one from God.
verses.4:6: Now these things, brothers, I have applied figuratively to myself and Apollos on your account, so that in us you may learn, "Not beyond what is written," so that none of you may be puffed up in favor of one against another.
verses.4:7: For who makes you distinct? And what do you possess that you did not receive? And if indeed you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
verses.4:8: Already you are satisfied, already you have become rich, apart from us you have begun to reign! And if only you really had begun to reign, so that we too might reign alongside you.
verses.4:9: For I suppose God has displayed us apostles as last, like those condemned to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to people.
verses.4:10: We are fools on account of Christ, but you are sensible in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honored, but we are without honor.
verses.4:11: Up to this very hour we both hunger and thirst, we go poorly clothed, we are struck with fists, we are homeless,
verses.4:12: and we toil, working with our own hands. When reviled, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;
verses.4:13: when slandered, we speak kindly. We have become like the refuse of the world, the scrapings of all things up to this moment.
verses.4:14: I am not writing these things to shame you, but I am admonishing you as my beloved children.
verses.4:15: For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I fathered you through the gospel.
verses.4:16: Therefore I urge you: become imitators of me.
verses.4:17: For this reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
verses.4:18: Now some have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.
verses.4:19: Yet I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of those who are puffed up, but their power,
verses.4:20: for the kingdom of God is not in talk, but in power.
verses.4:21: What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?
verses.5:1: Sexual immorality is actually being reported among you, and a kind of sexual immorality that does not occur even among the Gentiles: that someone has his father's wife.
verses.5:2: And you are puffed up, and have you not rather mourned, so that the one who did this deed would be taken away from your midst?
verses.5:3: For I, absent in body yet present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, the one who has done this in such a way,
verses.5:4: in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are assembled together along with my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
verses.5:5: to hand such a person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.
verses.5:6: Your boast is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the entire batch of dough?
verses.5:7: Clean out the old leaven, so that you may be a new batch of dough, just as you are unleavened. For indeed our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed.
verses.5:8: So then let us observe the festival, not with old leaven nor with the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
verses.5:9: I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral people,
verses.5:10: not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, for then you would indeed have to go out of the world.
verses.5:11: But as it is, I am writing to you not to associate with anyone bearing the name of brother if he is sexually immoral, or greedy, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or a swindler—not even to eat with such a one.
verses.5:12: For what is it to me to judge those outside? Do you not judge those inside,
verses.5:13: whereas God judges those outside? Drive out the evil person from among yourselves.
verses.6:1: Does any one of you, having a dispute against another, dare to be judged before the unrighteous rather than before the saints?
verses.6:2: Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy of the smallest legal cases?
verses.6:3: Do you not know that we will judge angels—how much more the things of this life?
verses.6:4: So if you have legal cases concerning this life, do you seat as judges those who are of no account in the church?
verses.6:5: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not one wise person among you who will be able to decide between his brothers,
verses.6:6: but brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers?
verses.6:7: Indeed, then, it is already a complete defeat for you that you have lawsuits against one another. Why do you not rather suffer wrong? Why do you not rather be defrauded?
verses.6:8: Instead, you yourselves do wrong and defraud—and brothers at that!
verses.6:9: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit God's kingdom? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate men, nor men who lie with males,
verses.6:10: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.6:11: And some of you were these things; yet you were washed, yet you were sanctified, yet you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
verses.6:12: "All things are permitted for me," yet not all things are beneficial. "All things are permitted for me," yet I myself will not be mastered by anything.
verses.6:13: "Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food," yet God will abolish both it and them. The body, however, is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body.
verses.6:14: And God both raised the Lord and will raise us up through His power.
verses.6:15: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Should I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? By no means!
verses.6:16: Or do you not know that the one who unites himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For "The two," He says, "will become one flesh."
verses.6:17: Yet the one who unites himself to the Lord is one spirit with Him.
verses.6:18: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, yet the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
verses.6:19: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
verses.6:20: for you were bought with a price. Glorify God, then, in your body.
verses.7:1: Now concerning the matters about which you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
verses.7:2: But because of acts of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
verses.7:3: Let the husband fulfill his duty to his wife, and likewise the wife also to her husband.
verses.7:4: The wife does not exercise authority over her own body, rather the husband does; and in the same way the husband also does not exercise authority over his own body, rather the wife does.
verses.7:5: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer and be together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
verses.7:6: Now I say this by way of concession, not as a command.
verses.7:7: Yet I wish that all people were even as I myself am; however, each person has his own gift from God, one in this way, and another in that.
verses.7:8: Now to the unmarried and to the widows I say: it is good for them if they remain even as I am;
verses.7:9: but if they do not exercise self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
verses.7:10: Now to the married I command, not I, but the Lord, that a wife is not to separate from her husband—
verses.7:11: yet if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and that a husband is not to divorce his wife.
verses.7:12: But to the rest I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to live with him, let him not divorce her.
verses.7:13: And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to live with her, let her not divorce her husband.
verses.7:14: For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified through his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified through the brother; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
verses.7:15: Yet if the unbeliever separates, let him separate. The brother or the sister is not bound in such cases; rather, God has called us in peace.
verses.7:16: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
verses.7:17: Only, as the Lord has assigned to each one, as God has called each one, in that manner let him walk. And so I direct in all the churches.
verses.7:18: Was anyone called while circumcised? Let him not undo his circumcision. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
verses.7:19: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but rather the keeping of God's commandments.
verses.7:20: Let each person remain in the calling in which he was called.
verses.7:21: Were you called as a slave? Do not let it concern you; yet if you are even able to become free, rather make use of it.
verses.7:22: For the one who was called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord's freedman; likewise the one who was called as a free person is a slave of Christ.
verses.7:23: You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of human beings.
verses.7:24: Brothers, in whatever situation each one was called, let him remain in that with God.
verses.7:25: Now concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord, yet I give my judgment as one who has been shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
verses.7:26: Therefore I consider this to be good because of the present distress: that it is good for a person to be as he is.
verses.7:27: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
verses.7:28: Yet even if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. However, such people will have affliction in the flesh, and I am seeking to spare you.
verses.7:29: Now this I say, brothers: the time has been shortened. From now on, let even those who have wives be as though they had none,
verses.7:30: and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,
verses.7:31: and those who use the world as though not making full use of it; for the form of this world is passing away.
verses.7:32: Now I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
verses.7:33: but the married man is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife, and he is divided. And the unmarried woman, as well as the virgin
verses.7:34: who is unmarried, is concerned about the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the married woman is concerned about the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
verses.7:35: Now I say this for your own benefit, not to put a restraint on you, but for what is proper and for devoted attendance to the Lord without distraction.
verses.7:36: But if anyone thinks that he is acting improperly toward his virgin if she is past her prime, and so it ought to be, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin; let them marry.
verses.7:37: But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity, and has authority over his own will, and has decided this in his own heart, to keep his own virgin, will do well.
verses.7:38: So then, both the one who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage will do better.
verses.7:39: A wife is bound for as long as her husband lives; but if her husband falls asleep, she is free to be married to whomever she wishes, only in the Lord.
verses.7:40: Yet she is more blessed if she remains as she is, according to my judgment; and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.
verses.8:1: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
verses.8:2: If anyone supposes that he has come to know anything, he has not yet known as he ought to know;
verses.8:3: but if anyone loves God, this person is known by Him.
verses.8:4: Therefore, concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God except one.
verses.8:5: For even if indeed there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—just as there are many gods and many lords—
verses.8:6: yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we are for Him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we are through Him.
verses.8:7: However, this knowledge is not in everyone; rather, some, through being accustomed to the idol until now, eat it as something sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
verses.8:8: Now food will not commend us to God; neither do we have an advantage if we eat, nor are we lacking if we do not eat.
verses.8:9: But take care that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
verses.8:10: For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, since he is weak, be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?
verses.8:11: For through your knowledge the one who is weak is destroyed, the brother for whom Christ died.
verses.8:12: And thus, by sinning against the brothers and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.
verses.8:13: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will certainly never eat meat, so that I will not cause my brother to stumble.
verses.9:1: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? You are my work in the Lord, are you not?
verses.9:2: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least to you I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
verses.9:3: My defense to those who examine me is this.
verses.9:4: Do we not have the right to eat and to drink?
verses.9:5: Do we not have the right to take along a sister as a wife, just as the rest of the apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas also do?
verses.9:6: Or is it only Barnabas and I who do not have the right to refrain from working?
verses.9:7: Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not eat from the milk of the flock?
verses.9:8: Am I speaking these things in human terms, or does the law not say these things also?
verses.9:9: For in the law of Moses it is written, "You shall not muzzle a threshing ox." Is God concerned about oxen,
verses.9:10: or does He speak altogether for our sake? For it was written for our sake, because the one who plows ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes, in hope of sharing.
verses.9:11: If we sowed spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap material things from you?
verses.9:12: If others share in this right over you, do we not all the more? Yet we did not use this right, but we endure all things so that we may cause no hindrance to the gospel of Christ.
verses.9:13: Do you not know that those who perform sacred duties eat the things from the temple, and those who attend at the altar share with the altar?
verses.9:14: In the same way, the Lord also directed those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.
verses.9:15: But I have made use of none of these things. And I did not write these things so that it might be done this way for me; for it would be better for me to die than—no one will make my boast empty.
verses.9:16: For if I proclaim the gospel, I have no ground for boasting, for necessity is laid upon me; for woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel.
verses.9:17: For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.
verses.9:18: What then is my reward? That in proclaiming the gospel I may present the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.
verses.9:19: For though I am free from all, I enslaved myself to all, so that I might gain the more.
verses.9:20: And to the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might gain Jews; to those under the law, as one under the law—though not myself under the law—so that I might gain those under the law;
verses.9:21: to those without the law, as one without the law—not being without the law of God, but within the law of Christ—so that I might gain those without the law.
verses.9:22: To the weak I became weak, so that I might gain the weak; I have become all things to all people, so that by every means I might save some.
verses.9:23: And I do all things for the sake of the gospel, so that I may become a fellow sharer in it.
verses.9:24: Do you not know that those who run in a stadium all run, yet one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
verses.9:25: And everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things; they do so to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable one.
verses.9:26: Therefore I run in this way, not aimlessly; I box in this way, not as one beating the air;
verses.9:27: but I bruise my body and bring it into slavery, so that after proclaiming to others, I myself may not somehow become disqualified.
verses.10:1: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
verses.10:2: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
verses.10:3: and all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.10:4: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they were drinking from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
verses.10:5: Yet with most of them God was not well pleased, for they were laid low in the wilderness.
verses.10:6: Now these things became examples for us, so that we would not crave evil things, just as they also craved them.
verses.10:7: And do not become idolaters, as some of them did; just as it is written, "The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play."
verses.10:8: Nor let us practice sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
verses.10:9: Nor let us put the Lord to the test, as some of them tested Him and were destroyed by the serpents.
verses.10:10: And do not grumble, just as some of them grumbled and perished by the destroyer.
verses.10:11: Now these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
verses.10:12: So then, let the one who thinks he is standing watch out that he does not fall.
verses.10:13: No temptation has taken hold of you except what is common to humanity; and God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but along with the temptation will also make the way out, so that you may be able to bear up under it.
verses.10:14: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
verses.10:15: I speak as to discerning people; judge for yourselves what I say.
verses.10:16: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ?
verses.10:17: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake from the one bread.
verses.10:18: Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?
verses.10:19: What then am I saying? That food sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
verses.10:20: No, but that the things the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become participants with demons.
verses.10:21: You cannot drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons; you cannot share in the Lord's table and the table of demons.
verses.10:22: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? We are not stronger than He is, are we?
verses.10:23: All things are permissible, yet not all things are beneficial. All things are permissible, yet not all things build up.
verses.10:24: Let no one seek his own good, but that of the other.
verses.10:25: Eat everything sold in the meat market without raising any question for the sake of conscience,
verses.10:26: for the earth belongs to the Lord, and its fullness.
verses.10:27: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you without raising any question for the sake of conscience.
verses.10:28: But if anyone says to you, "This was offered in sacrifice," do not eat it, for the sake of the one who pointed it out and for the sake of conscience—
verses.10:29: I mean not your own conscience, but that of the other person. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?
verses.10:30: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I spoken evil of concerning that for which I give thanks?
verses.10:31: Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do everything to the glory of God.
verses.10:32: Give no cause for stumbling either to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God,
verses.10:33: just as I also please everyone in everything, not seeking my own benefit, but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
verses.11:1: Become imitators of me, just as I also am of Christ.
verses.11:2: Now I commend you because you remember me in all things and hold firmly to the traditions just as I handed them down to you.
verses.11:3: Yet I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
verses.11:4: Every man who prays or prophesies with something over his head disgraces his head.
verses.11:5: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head, for it is one and the same thing as a woman whose head is shaved.
verses.11:6: For if a woman is not covered, let her also have her hair cut short; but if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut short or to be shaved, let her be covered.
verses.11:7: For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.
verses.11:8: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
verses.11:9: for indeed man was not created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man.
verses.11:10: Therefore the woman ought to have authority on her head because of the angels.
verses.11:11: Nevertheless, neither is woman apart from man nor man apart from woman in the Lord;
verses.11:12: for just as the woman is from the man, so also the man is through the woman; yet all things are from God.
verses.11:13: Judge among yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
verses.11:14: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him,
verses.11:15: but if a woman wears long hair, it is a glory to her? For her long hair has been given to her in place of a covering.
verses.11:16: Now if anyone seems inclined to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
verses.11:17: Now in giving this instruction, I do not commend you, because you come together not for the better, but for the worse.
verses.11:18: For in the first place, when you come together as a church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and in part I believe it.
verses.11:19: For there must also be factions among you, so that those who are approved may also become evident among you.
verses.11:20: Therefore, when you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's supper,
verses.11:21: for in eating, each one goes ahead with his own supper, and one goes hungry while another gets drunk.
verses.11:22: Do you not indeed have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the church of God and disgrace those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I commend you? In this I do not commend you.
verses.11:23: For I received from the Lord what I also handed down to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was betrayed, took bread,
verses.11:24: and after giving thanks, He broke it and said, "This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:25: In the same way He also took the cup after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:26: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until He comes.
verses.11:27: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty concerning the body and the blood of the Lord.
verses.11:28: But let a person examine himself, and in that way let him eat from the bread and drink from the cup;
verses.11:29: for the one who eats and drinks eats and drinks judgment upon himself, not discerning the body.
verses.11:30: Because of this, many among you are weak and sick, and a considerable number are asleep.
verses.11:31: But if we carefully judged ourselves, we would not be judged;
verses.11:32: yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
verses.11:33: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
verses.11:34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you will not come together for judgment. And the remaining matters I will arrange whenever I come.
verses.12:1: Now concerning spiritual matters, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.
verses.12:2: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.
verses.12:3: Therefore I am making known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed," and no one is able to say, "Jesus is Lord," except in the Holy Spirit.
verses.12:4: Now there are varieties of gifts, yet the same Spirit;
verses.12:5: and there are varieties of services, and the same Lord;
verses.12:6: and there are varieties of workings, yet the same God who works all things in all.
verses.12:7: Now to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
verses.12:8: For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
verses.12:9: to another faith in the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings in the one Spirit,
verses.12:10: and to another workings of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discernments of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues;
verses.12:11: but one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing individually to each one just as He wills.
verses.12:12: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though being many, are one body, so also is Christ.
verses.12:13: For indeed in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
verses.12:14: For indeed the body is not one member, but many.
verses.12:15: If the foot says, "Because I am not a hand, I am not part of the body," is it for that reason not part of the body?
verses.12:16: And if the ear says, "Because I am not an eye, I am not part of the body," it is not for that reason any less part of the body.
verses.12:17: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
verses.12:18: But as it is, God placed the members, each one of them, in the body just as He desired.
verses.12:19: And if they were all one member, where would the body be?
verses.12:20: But as it is, there are many members, yet one body.
verses.12:21: And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," or again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
verses.12:22: On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are all the more necessary,
verses.12:23: and those parts of the body that we think to be less honorable, on these we bestow greater honor, and our unpresentable parts have greater decorum,
verses.12:24: whereas our presentable parts have no need of it. Rather, God has blended the body together, giving greater honor to the part that lacks it,
verses.12:25: so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.
verses.12:26: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if a member is honored, all the members rejoice together.
verses.12:27: Now you are Christ's body, and individually members of it.
verses.12:28: And God has appointed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, and kinds of tongues.
verses.12:29: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all perform miracles?
verses.12:30: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
verses.12:31: But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And furthermore, I show you a surpassing way.
verses.13:1: If I speak in the tongues of people and of angels, but do not have love, I have become resounding bronze or a clashing cymbal.
verses.13:2: And if I have prophecy and understand all the mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
verses.13:3: And if I dole out all my possessions, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
verses.13:4: Love is patient, love is kind, love does not envy, does not brag, is not puffed up,
verses.13:5: does not behave improperly, does not seek its own, is not provoked, does not keep count of wrong,
verses.13:6: does not rejoice over unrighteousness, but rejoices together with the truth;
verses.13:7: it bears up under all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
verses.13:8: Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will be brought to an end; whether tongues, they will cease; whether knowledge, it will be brought to an end.
verses.13:9: For in part we know, and in part we prophesy;
verses.13:10: but when what is complete comes, what is in part will be brought to an end.
verses.13:11: When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child; when I became a man, I put an end to the things of a child.
verses.13:12: For at present we see through a mirror indistinctly, but then face to face; at present I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I also was fully known.
verses.13:13: But now faith, hope, love remain, these three; and the greatest of these is love.
verses.14:1: Pursue love, and eagerly desire spiritual things, but especially that you may prophesy.
verses.14:2: For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people, but to God, for no one understands; instead, in spirit he speaks mysteries.
verses.14:3: But the one who prophesies speaks to people building up, encouragement, and consolation.
verses.14:4: The one who speaks in a tongue builds himself up, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.
verses.14:5: Now I wish for all of you to speak in tongues, but even more that you may prophesy; and the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building up.
verses.14:6: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation or in knowledge or in prophecy or in teaching?
verses.14:7: Even lifeless things that give a sound, whether flute or harp, if they do not give a distinction in the tones, how will what is played on the flute or what is played on the harp be known?
verses.14:8: For indeed, if a trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will prepare himself for battle?
verses.14:9: So also you, unless with the tongue you give intelligible speech, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into the air.
verses.14:10: There are, perhaps, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning;
verses.14:11: if then I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the one who speaks, and the one who speaks will be a foreigner to me.
verses.14:12: So also you, since you are zealous for spirits, seek to abound for the building up of the church.
verses.14:13: Therefore, let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
verses.14:14: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
verses.14:15: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the mind also; I will sing praise with the spirit, and I will sing praise with the mind also.
verses.14:16: Otherwise, if you bless in spirit, how will the one who fills the place of the uninstructed person say the "Amen" at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
verses.14:17: For you indeed give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.
verses.14:18: I give thanks to God, I speak in tongues more than all of you;
verses.14:19: yet in church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I may instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verses.14:20: Brothers, do not become children in your thinking; instead, be infants in evil, and in your thinking become mature.
verses.14:21: In the law it is written, "By people of other tongues and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people, and not even so will they listen to Me," says the Lord.
verses.14:22: So then, tongues are for a sign, not for those who believe but for unbelievers; while prophecy is not for unbelievers but for those who believe.
verses.14:23: Therefore, if the whole church comes together in one place and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed people or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
verses.14:24: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in, he is convicted by all, he is examined by all,
verses.14:25: the secrets of his heart become manifest, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God, declaring, "Truly God is among you."
verses.14:26: What is it then, brothers? Whenever you come together, each one has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up.
verses.14:27: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be two, or at most three, and each in turn, and let one interpret;
verses.14:28: but if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
verses.14:29: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern;
verses.14:30: but if something is revealed to another who is seated, let the first keep silent.
verses.14:31: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged
verses.14:32: (and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets,
verses.14:33: for God is not a God of disorder but of peace), as in all the churches of the saints.
verses.14:34: Let the women keep silent in the churches, for it is not permitted for them to speak; rather, let them be in subjection, just as the law also says.
verses.14:35: And if they desire to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is disgraceful for a woman to speak in church.
verses.14:36: Or did the word of God go out from you, or did it reach you alone?
verses.14:37: If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize that the things I am writing to you are the Lord's: a command.
verses.14:38: But if anyone is ignorant, let him remain ignorant.
verses.14:39: So then, my brothers, eagerly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues;
verses.14:40: but let all things be done properly and in an orderly manner.
verses.15:1: Now I make known to you, brothers, the gospel that I preached to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
verses.15:2: and through which you are also being saved, if you hold firmly to the word by which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
verses.15:3: For I handed down to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:4: and that He was buried, and that He has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:5: and that He appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
verses.15:6: After that He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at a single time, most of whom remain until now, though some have fallen asleep.
verses.15:7: After that He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
verses.15:8: And last of all, as to one born prematurely, He appeared also to me.
verses.15:9: For I am the least of the apostles, not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
verses.15:10: But by God's grace I am what I am, and His grace toward me did not turn out empty; instead, I labored more abundantly than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me.
verses.15:11: Whether then it is I or they, this is how we proclaim, and this is how you believed.
verses.15:12: Now if Christ is proclaimed that He has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.15:13: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then neither has Christ been raised;
verses.15:14: and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your faith is also empty.
verses.15:15: Moreover, we are even found to be false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that He raised Christ, whom He did not raise if indeed the dead are not raised.
verses.15:16: For if the dead are not raised, then neither has Christ been raised;
verses.15:17: and if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
verses.15:18: Then those also who fell asleep in Christ have perished.
verses.15:19: If we have hoped in Christ in this life only, we are more to be pitied than all people.
verses.15:20: Now, however, Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
verses.15:21: For since death came through a man, through a man also comes the resurrection of the dead.
verses.15:22: For just as all die in Adam, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
verses.15:23: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then those who belong to Christ at His coming.
verses.15:24: Then comes the end, when He hands over the kingdom to the God and Father, once He has abolished every rule and every authority and power.
verses.15:25: For He must reign until He places all enemies under His feet.
verses.15:26: The last enemy to be abolished is death;
verses.15:27: for He has subjected all things under His feet. But when it says, "All things have been subjected," it is clear that this excludes the One who subjected all things to Him.
verses.15:28: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will also be subjected to the One who subjected all things to Him, so that God may be all in all.
verses.15:29: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are they even baptized on behalf of them?
verses.15:30: Why are we also in danger every hour?
verses.15:31: I die every day, by the boasting about you, brothers, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord!
verses.15:32: If in human terms I fought wild beasts in Ephesus, what is the benefit to me? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
verses.15:33: Do not be deceived: bad associations corrupt good character.
verses.15:34: Sober up properly and stop sinning, for some have no knowledge of God; I speak to your shame.
verses.15:35: But someone will say, "How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?"
verses.15:36: Foolish one! What you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
verses.15:37: And what you sow—you do not sow the body that will come into being, but a bare grain, perhaps of wheat or of some other kind.
verses.15:38: But God gives it a body just as He willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.
verses.15:39: Not all flesh is the same flesh, but there is one kind for humans, another flesh for animals, another flesh for birds, and another for fish.
verses.15:40: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; yet the glory of the heavenly is one thing, and the glory of the earthly is another.
verses.15:41: The sun has one glory, the moon another glory, and the stars another glory; for one star differs from another star in glory.
verses.15:42: So it is with the resurrection of the dead as well. It is sown in perishability; it is raised in imperishability.
verses.15:43: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
verses.15:44: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual one.
verses.15:45: Thus it is also written: "The first man, Adam, became a living soul"; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
verses.15:46: However, the spiritual does not come first, but the natural, and after that the spiritual.
verses.15:47: The first man is from the earth, made of dust; the second man is from heaven.
verses.15:48: Just as the one made of dust is, so also are those made of dust; and just as the heavenly One is, so also are those who are heavenly.
verses.15:49: And just as we have borne the image of the one made of dust, let us also bear the image of the heavenly One.
verses.15:50: Now I say this, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does perishability inherit imperishability.
verses.15:51: Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all fall asleep, but we will all be changed,
verses.15:52: in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
verses.15:53: For this perishable must clothe itself with imperishability, and this mortal must clothe itself with immortality.
verses.15:54: And when this perishable clothes itself with imperishability, and this mortal clothes itself with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
verses.15:55: "Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?"
verses.15:56: Now the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law;
verses.15:57: yet thanks be to God, the One who grants us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:58: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be firm, immovable, always overflowing in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.
verses.16:1: Now concerning the collection for the saints, just as I directed the churches of Galatia, you also are to do so.
verses.16:2: On the first day of every week, let each one of you set something aside on his own, storing it up as he may prosper, so that no collections will be made when I come.
verses.16:3: And when I arrive, whomever you approve by letters, these I will send to carry your gift to Jerusalem;
verses.16:4: and if it is worthwhile for me to go as well, they will go with me.
verses.16:5: Now I will come to you once I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia,
verses.16:6: and with you perhaps I will stay, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I may go.
verses.16:7: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, for I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
verses.16:8: Yet I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost;
verses.16:9: for a wide and effective door stands open for me, and there are many opponents.
verses.16:10: Now if Timothy comes, see to it that he is without fear among you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, as I am.
verses.16:11: Therefore let no one treat him with contempt. Rather, send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.
verses.16:12: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers; yet it was not at all the will that he come now, but he will come when he has an opportunity.
verses.16:13: Keep watch, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, be strong.
verses.16:14: Let everything of yours be done in love.
verses.16:15: Now I urge you, brothers (you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to service for the saints),
verses.16:16: that you also be subject to such people, and to everyone who works together and labors.
verses.16:17: And I rejoice at the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these men have supplied what was lacking from you,
verses.16:18: for they refreshed both my spirit and yours. Therefore recognize such people.
verses.16:19: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, along with the church in their house.
verses.16:20: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.16:21: The greeting is by my own hand—Paul's.
verses.16:22: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. Marana tha.
verses.16:23: May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.16:24: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

notes.1:2: The Greek text places "those sanctified in Christ Jesus" before "that is in Corinth," and "both theirs and ours" at the end of the verse can grammatically modify either "every place" or "our Lord Jesus Christ."
notes.1:14: The critical Greek text reads simply "I give thanks," omitting "to God," which is added in many later manuscripts.
notes.1:23: The critical Greek text reads "Gentiles" (literally "nations") here rather than "Greeks," which appears in some later manuscripts in assimilation to verses 22 and 24.
notes.1:30: The particles te kai ... kai bind righteousness, sanctification, and redemption closely together; they may explain "wisdom from God" or stand alongside it.
notes.2:1: The critical Greek text reads "testimony" (martyrion), though several early witnesses read "mystery" (mysterion), likely influenced by verse 7.
notes.2:10: The critical Greek text reads "For" rather than "But" and "through the Spirit" without the possessive pronoun "His" found in some later manuscripts.
notes.2:13: The final Greek clause is syntactically ambiguous and may be understood either as "interpreting spiritual things to spiritual people" (masculine dative) or as "explaining spiritual realities with spiritual words" (neuter dative).
notes.2:14: The Greek adjective psychikos ("natural") literally denotes a person living by the natural soul and human faculties apart from the Spirit of God.
notes.3:1: Paul uses sarkinos ("of flesh") here before shifting to the related adjective sarkikos ("fleshly") in verse 3.
notes.3:4: The critical Greek text reads "human beings" rather than "fleshly," which appears in some later manuscripts under the influence of verse 3.
notes.3:9: "God's fellow workers" can mean either coworkers who belong to God or workers who labor in partnership with God.
notes.3:16: "Temple" translates naos, the inner sanctuary where God's presence dwells, and "you" is plural throughout verses 16-17, referring to the church collectively.
notes.4:3: "Human court" translates Greek anthropines hemeras, literally "a human day," referring to a day of human judicial reckoning in contrast to the coming day of the Lord.
notes.4:6: The phrase "Not beyond what is written" has no verb in the Greek, and its exact reference is debated, most likely pointing back to the Scripture passages cited in chapters 1-3 or to a familiar maxim about keeping within scriptural boundaries.
notes.4:15: Greek paidagogous refers to household guardians who supervised and escorted children rather than formal schoolteachers, contrasted here with a father.
notes.5:4: "In the name of our Lord Jesus" may grammatically modify Paul's judgment (v. 3), the congregation's gathering (v. 4), or the handing over of the offender (v. 5).
notes.5:5: "Destruction of the flesh" is debated, understood either as severe physical affliction or death, or as the breaking of the person's sinful fleshly impulses so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
notes.5:13: Greek krinei is accented as present tense ("judges"), though unaccented manuscripts can also be read as future ("will judge"). The final command echoes Deuteronomy 17:7.
notes.6:4: Greek kathizete may be taken either as an indicative question ("do you seat...?") referring to pagan judges who hold no standing in the church, or as an ironic imperative referring to the least esteemed believers.
notes.6:9: Greek malakoi (literally "soft ones") and arsenokoitai (a compound of "male" and "bed") are commonly understood as the passive and active partners in male same-sex intercourse, though their precise sense is debated.
notes.6:12: Quotation marks here and in verse 13 do not appear in Greek manuscripts; they reflect the widespread view that Paul is quoting and qualifying Corinthian slogans.
notes.6:18: Literally "Every sin"; some interpreters read the first clause as another Corinthian slogan that Paul refutes, while others take it as Paul's own statement.
notes.7:1: The clause "it is good for a man not to touch a woman" is widely understood as a slogan quoted from the Corinthians' letter, with "touch" used as a euphemism for sexual relations.
notes.7:21: The Greek imperative translated "make use of it" has no explicit object; interpreters debate whether Paul urges slaves to take the opportunity to become free or to make use of their present condition.
notes.7:33: Manuscript wording and punctuation vary here; the Greek source concludes the sentence about the married man with "and he is divided" and continues with "the unmarried woman" and "the virgin who is unmarried" across vv. 33-34.
notes.7:36: Interpreters debate whether "his virgin" refers to a father's unmarried daughter or a man's betrothed fiancée, and whether the Greek term translated "past her prime" refers to her age or to his strong passions.
notes.8:1: The assertion "we all have knowledge" (along with the claims in v. 4) is widely regarded as a Corinthian slogan that Paul quotes and then qualifies.
notes.8:8: The Greek source places the clause regarding eating before the clause regarding not eating, the reverse of the order found in some other manuscripts.
notes.8:10: The verb "be built up" ironically echoes "builds up" in v. 1, indicating that a weak believer's conscience could be emboldened to act contrary to its own convictions.
notes.9:5: Literally 'a sister, a wife,' referring to a Christian wife accompanying an apostle in his travels.
notes.9:15: The Greek sentence breaks off abruptly after 'than' (anacoluthon), reflecting Paul's emphatic shift to declare that no one will make his boast empty.
notes.9:21: Paul plays on the Greek terms anomos ('without the law') and ennomos ('within the law') to clarify that living apart from the Mosaic law does not mean being lawless toward God, since he lives under Christ's law.
notes.9:27: The verb translated 'bruise' (hypopiazo) literally means 'strike under the eye,' continuing the boxing metaphor from v. 26, and 'proclaiming' (keryxas) can also evoke the herald at the athletic games.
notes.10:4: Paul draws on a Jewish interpretive tradition that the water-giving rock of Exodus 17 and Numbers 20 accompanied Israel in the wilderness, identifying its spiritual reality with Christ.
notes.10:8: Numbers 25:9 gives the number of those who died in the plague as 24,000.
notes.10:9: The Greek source text reads 'the Lord' (ton Kyrion), while many ancient manuscripts read 'Christ' (ton Christon) and a few read 'God' (ton theon).
notes.10:28: The speaker uses the neutral term hierothyton ('offered in sacrifice') rather than Paul's term eidōlothyton ('sacrificed to idols', v. 19). Later manuscripts repeat v. 26 at the end of this verse, which is omitted in the earliest witnesses.
notes.11:3: Greek aner and gyne can mean "man/woman" or "husband/wife," and the metaphorical sense of kephale ("head") is debated between authority and source.
notes.11:4: Greek kata kephales echon is literally "having [something] down from his head," referring to a head covering.
notes.11:10: Greek exousian echein epi tes kephales is literally "to have authority on her head," variously understood as a sign of authority over her or her own authority to pray and prophesy.
notes.11:24: The critical Greek text reads simply "which is for you," omitting the later manuscript addition "broken" (klomenon).
notes.11:29: The critical Greek text omits "in an unworthy manner" and "of the Lord" found in later manuscripts; "the body" may refer to Christ's eucharistic body, the gathered church, or both.
notes.12:1: Greek ton pneumatikon can be read as neuter ("spiritual matters" or "spiritual gifts") or masculine ("spiritual persons").
notes.12:2: The Greek syntax is elliptical, conveying that before conversion the Corinthians were repeatedly carried off to mute idols by whatever impulse led them.
notes.12:13: Greek en heni pneumati may be understood either locatively ("in one Spirit") or instrumentally ("by one Spirit").
notes.12:31: Greek zeloute has the same form in the imperative ("earnestly desire") and the indicative ("you are earnestly desiring").
notes.13:3: The Greek text reads ἵνα καυχήσωμαι ('so that I may boast'), supported by early Alexandrian witnesses (P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus); other manuscripts read καυθήσωμαι ('so that I may be burned').
notes.13:10: Greek τὸ τέλειον ('what is complete' or 'the perfect') contrasts directly with τὸ ἐκ μέρους ('what is in part').
notes.13:12: Greek ἐν αἰνίγματι literally means 'in a riddle' (cf. Numbers 12:8 LXX), conveying an obscure or indistinct reflection as viewed in an ancient metal mirror.
notes.14:12: Greek πνευμάτων literally means 'spirits,' referring in this context to spiritual gifts or manifestations.
notes.14:33: The punctuation places verses 32-33a in parentheses, connecting 'as in all the churches of the saints' to verse 31; many editions and interpreters instead attach that clause to the beginning of verse 34.
notes.14:34: Some Western manuscripts place verses 34-35 after verse 40 rather than here, a variation widely discussed in textual criticism.
notes.14:37: The Greek text reads singular ἐντολή ('a command') following κυρίου ἐστίν ('are the Lord's'); other manuscripts read plural ἐντολαί ('commands') or omit the word.
notes.14:38: The Greek text reads the active imperative ἀγνοείτω ('let him remain ignorant'); other manuscripts read the passive indicative ἀγνοεῖται ('he is not recognized').
notes.15:8: The Greek term ektrōmati (with the definite article) literally denotes a miscarriage or an abnormally early birth.
notes.15:29: The phrase "baptized on behalf of the dead" (hyper tōn nekrōn) is famously debated, with proposals ranging from vicarious baptism for deceased persons to baptism undertaken in hope of rejoining dead believers.
notes.15:44: Greek psychikon literally means "soulish" (pertaining to the psychē, natural mortal life), contrasted with pneumatikon ("spiritual").
notes.15:49: The critical Greek text reads the hortatory subjunctive phoresōmen ("let us also bear"), supported by strong early manuscripts; other manuscripts read the future indicative phoresomen ("we will also bear"), which aligns with the predictive statements in the context.
notes.16:3: The phrase "by letters" (di' epistolon) may modify either "approve" (following the punctuation here) or "send" ("these I will send with letters"). "Gift" translates charis (lit. "grace"), used here for the charitable contribution.
notes.16:12: The Greek literally reads "it was not at all a will" (ouk en thelema) without a possessive pronoun, leaving open whether Paul refers to Apollos's own desire or to God's will.
notes.16:13: "Be courageous" translates andrizesthe (lit. "act like men"), an established Greek and Septuagint idiom for displaying courage and resolve.
notes.16:22: "Marana tha" is an Aramaic invocation transliterated in Greek meaning "Our Lord, come!" (divided differently as Maran atha, it can mean "Our Lord has come").
